verdict.label: Light review
verdict.summary: Create an OAuth 2.0 Web App or Automated App/bot in the X Developer Console, configure PKCE and redirect URIs, and connect via Composio.
verdict.cost: Pay-per-use credits (per-endpoint pricing in the Developer Console)

composioFit.summary: X requires bringing your own OAuth app because Composio-managed OAuth is not available for Twitter/X.
whyOwnApp: Brings dedicated quota instead of shared provider quotas
Allows custom branding, scopes, and direct API credential management

phases.name: Create Developer App
steps: Go to the X Developer Console.
Create a new App and choose OAuth 2.0 with a confidential client type (Web App or Automated App/bot).
phases.handoff: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into your secure configuration or Composio auth config.

phases.name: Configure Redirect URIs and Scopes
steps: Enable OAuth 2.0 in your App's authentication settings.
Add the exact callback URL provided by the Composio dashboard to your app's allowlist.
Select required fine-grained scopes such as tweet.read, users.read, and offline.access.
phases.handoff: Save settings in the Developer Console.

phases.name: Test Integration
steps: Initiate the OAuth flow using PKCE and your Client ID.
Exchange the authorization code within 30 seconds for an access token and refresh token.
Verify API connectivity using v2 endpoints.
phases.handoff: Verify successful account connection in Composio.

artefacts.title: X App Configuration Form Values
artefacts.body:
App Name: My AI Agent X Integration
App Type: Web App or Automated App / Bot (Confidential Client)
Callback URL: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>
Scopes Needed: tweet.read, tweet.write, users.read, offline.access

artefacts.title: Scope Justification
artefacts.body: The AI agent requires tweet.read and users.read to retrieve public context and user timeline information, tweet.write to publish agent responses on behalf of the user, and offline.access to maintain a persistent connection via refresh tokens without requiring repeated user re-authentication.

artefacts.title: Privacy Policy & Terms Requirements
artefacts.body:
- Publish a public Privacy Policy URL detailing data collection and token handling.
- Publish Developer Terms acceptance.
- Ensure exact match validation on all registered callback URIs.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy
requirements.when: Required for application compliance and developer terms.

requirements.label: Callback URL Validation
requirements.when: Mandatory exact match validation for callback URLs.

requirements.label: Prepaid API credits
requirements.when: Before your agent can make API calls beyond any free credits

scopes.purpose: Read user account details and profile information
Issue a refresh token to obtain new access tokens without prompting the user

redirectRules.rule: Must use exact match validation for callback URLs
Maximum of 10 callback URLs per app
For local development, use http://127.0.0.1 instead of localhost

blockers.symptom: Calls fail once the app is live although OAuth succeeded
blockers.cause: X API is pay-per-use; requests deduct prepaid credits.
blockers.fix: Buy credits and set a spending limit / auto-recharge in the Developer Console; budget per endpoint.
blockers.fallback: Cache aggressively and call fewer, cheaper endpoints.

blockers.symptom: "message" : "Callback URL not approved for this client application."
blockers.cause: The redirect URI passed in the authorization request does not exactly match the callback URL registered in the Developer Console, including protocols and trailing slashes.
blockers.fix: Ensure your callback URL is exactly as registered in the Developer Console and properly HTTP-encoded when passing as a query parameter.
blockers.fallback: Re-verify allowed callback URLs in the App settings.

blockers.symptom: Authorization code invalid or expired error during token exchange.
blockers.cause: The auth_code has a time limit of 30 seconds once the App owner receives an approved auth_code from the user.
blockers.fix: Exchange the authorization code for an access token immediately within 30 seconds.
blockers.fallback: Restart the OAuth authorization flow to generate a fresh authorization code.

blockers.symptom: Redirect fails when testing locally using localhost.
blockers.cause: Using 'localhost' can cause validation failures with X callback rules.
blockers.fix: Use http://127.0.0.1 instead of localhost for local development.
blockers.fallback: Register http://127.0.0.1 explicitly in the allowed callback URLs.

checklist.text: Sign in to the X Developer Console and create a new App.
Select a confidential client app type such as Web App or Automated App/bot.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
Enable OAuth 2.0 in the App's authentication settings.
Add the Composio redirect URI to your app's allowlist using exact match validation.
Configure fine-grained scopes including tweet.read, users.read, and offline.access.
Initiate the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE.
Exchange the authorization code for tokens within the 30-second window.
Verify successful connection in the Composio dashboard.
